item.title: Teen Charged in Georgia School Shooting Changes Plea to Guilty
item.description: Colt Gray, 16, had been scheduled to go on trial in October. His change of plea took place at a hearing that pivoted immediately to sentencing.
item.dc:creator: Sean Keenan and Rick Rojas
item.media:credit: Amanda Kathleen Greene for The New York Times
item.media:description: Students, friends and family bring flowers and balloons, and gather at the flagpole in front of Apalachee High School in Winder, Ga. in 2024.

item.title: With Hopes High for New H.I.V. Prevention Pill, Merck Takes Steps to Ensure Access
item.description: Companies in Africa and India will make generic versions of the pill that could cost as little as $5 per person per year. But access to the drug and other new products in much of Latin America remains uncertain.
item.dc:creator: Stephanie Nolen
item.category: Far East, South and Southeast Asia and Pacific Areas
item.media:credit: Arlette Bashizi for The New York Times
item.media:description: Health workers speaking with students about H.I.V. prevention drugs at the University of Zambia in Lusaka in March.

item.title: Man in a Spider-Man Costume Rides to the Rescue in Arkansas
item.description: Was that Peter Parker helping a man in a wheelchair cross an intersection? No, it was Chris Hellenthal, a college student returning from a summer job.
item.dc:creator: Francesca Regalado

item.title: How a Grieving Trump Decided to Back Lindsey Graham’s Sister for Senate
item.description: The president initially backed a little-known congressman. Then he talked to Gov. Henry McMaster and Ms. Graham herself.
item.dc:creator: Emily Davies
item.media:description: Mr. Trump’s support for Darline Graham, the sister of the late senator Lindsey Graham but a political unknown, is a gamble as Republicans and Democrats battle for control of the House and Senate.

item.title: Black Parents Are Rattled by Mississippi Teen’s Death Among White Friends
item.description: The death of Nolan Wells after he boated with friends to an island party on July 4 has sparked anguish among Black parents about the safety of their children in predominantly white spaces.
item.dc:creator: Clyde McGrady
item.media:description: From left to right, Elmore Wonsley, Christine Wells-Wonsley and their lawyer, Ben Crump, at a news conference where Mr. Crump announced the results of an independent autopsy on Nolan Wells during the N.A.A.C.P. Convention in Chicago on Wednesday.

item.title: Democrats Prepare for Possible Election Clashes With Federal Government
item.description: Top officials overseeing state elections and law enforcement are stepping up plans to prepare for what they worry could be interference in the midterms.
item.dc:creator: Nick Corasaniti
item.media:credit: Philip Cheung for The New York Times
item.media:description: Democratic attorneys general and secretaries of state, who oversee law enforcement and elections in their states, are aiming to work more diligently together on elections.

item.title: After the Cesar Chavez Scandal, Can Johnny Itliong Restore His Father’s Activist Legacy?
item.description: Johnny Itliong says Cesar Chavez stole credit from his father, the farmworker activist Larry Itliong. For years, he has been trying to correct the record.
item.dc:creator: Jill Cowan and Mark Abramson for The New York Times
item.media:description: “I have been fighting to get the story of my father out for decades and have been waiting for the U.F.W. to step up and honor Larry as they do Cesar,” said Johnny Itliong, at a mural commemorating his father.

item.title: ICE Contractor Faces Charges in Shooting Outside Colorado Detention Center
item.description: The man, Brandon Booth, was also fired by the operator of the center, GEO Group, after a woman who was protesting outside was shot in the foot.
item.dc:creator: Mack Liederman and John S.W. MacDonald
item.media:description: Protesters last month outside the ICE processing center in Aurora, Colo.

item.title: Jackie, Bald Eagle and Webcam Star, Is Recovering After an Attack in California
item.description: Jackie found an online audience through a webcam pointed at her nest in California. She was rescued last week after a fight with other eagles, officials said.
item.dc:creator: Alexandra E. Petri

item.title: A Fallen Soldier’s Angst, Love and Longing to Return Home From the Iran War
item.description: Sgt. Michael Emmanuel Swinton was killed in recent days, one of 18 U.S. soldiers who have lost their lives since the beginning of the war in Iran.

item.title: Los Angeles Homeless Population Grows Again, After 2 Years of Decline
item.description: Los Angeles had an increase in homeless residents between early 2025 and early 2026. The rise could hurt Mayor Karen Bass, as she runs for re-election.
item.dc:creator: Jill Cowan and Shawn Hubler
item.media:credit: Kyle Grillot for The New York Times
item.media:description: Mayor Karen Bass had previously promoted declines in homelessness during her first two full years in office.

item.title: Kagan Says Supreme Court Has Stood Up to Trump in Key Cases
item.description: At an annual meeting of judges and lawyers, the liberal justice defended her conservative colleagues from criticism that they have rubber-stamped President Trump’s agenda.
item.dc:creator: Abbie VanSickle
item.media:description: Justice Elena Kagan testified alongside Justice Amy Coney Barrett on Capitol Hill earlier this month to request more money for security for the justices.

item.title: Democratic Voters Keep Defying the Party Establishment
item.description: The House Democratic campaign arm has stepped up its interventions in high-profile contested primaries. But this week, it suffered its third primary defeat in two months.
item.dc:creator: Katie Glueck
item.media:credit: Cassidy Araiza for The New York Times
item.media:description: Dr. Amish Shah, a moderate Democratic candidate for the House in Arizona, won a primary this week against a different moderate Democrat who was heavily backed by the House Democratic campaign arm.

item.title: A Lakers Jacket, Bought for $3 at Goodwill, Fetches Nearly $90,000 at Auction
item.description: Quinn Brown, a 19-year-old thrifter from Portland, Ore., bought a warm-up jacket worn by Wilt Chamberlain for $3.07. Six months later, Sotheby’s auctioned it off for $89,600.
item.dc:creator: John S.W. MacDonald

item.title: Trump and Thune Clash Over SAVE America Act

item.dc:creator: Michael Gold

item.title: Bear Dies After Getting Stranded Atop Electric Pole in New Mexico
item.description: The animal’s plight alarmed onlookers and highlighted the drought conditions that are forcing wild bears closer to where people live in search of food.
item.dc:creator: Michael Levenson

item.title: Tugboat Captain Pleads Guilty in Miami Crash That Killed 3 Children
item.description: Prosecutors said the captain’s view was blocked as the barge he was pushing struck a sailboat carrying young campers and a counselor on Biscayne Bay.
item.dc:creator: Mark Walker
item.media:description: A tugboat crashed into a stalled sailboat in Biscayne Bay near Miami Beach, Fla., last year, killing three girls who were 7, 10 and 13.

item.title: Clint Reilly, Political Consultant Known for Feuding, Dies at 79
item.description: As savvy as he could be volatile, he advised Nancy Pelosi and Dianne Feinstein, ran for mayor of San Francisco and bought The San Francisco Examiner.
item.dc:creator: Trip Gabriel
item.media:description: Clint Reilly at his San Francisco home in 1999, the year he ran unsuccessfully for mayor. He spent $3.5 million of his own money and finished fourth.

item.title: ICE Targets ‘Detention Desert’ With New Facility in North Carolina
item.description: Even as ICE has retreated from its plan to buy warehouses, the new complex near the Virginia border signals that the agency remains determined to increase its detention capacity.
item.dc:creator: Eduardo Medina and Hamed Aleaziz
item.media:credit: Cornell Watson for The New York Times
item.media:description: Internal documents obtained by The New York Times show that ICE plans to open a detention center at the old Rivers Correctional Institution in Winton, N.C., by the end of December.

item.title: Trump Administration Drops Subpoena Demanding List of Jews From Penn
item.description: The move was a rare pullback for the administration, which has used inquiries as leverage. Few schools resisted as Penn did after it was pressed for antisemitism complaints and a list of campus groups involved with Judaism.
item.dc:creator: Alan Blinder and Rebecca Davis O’Brien
item.media:credit: Hannah Beier for The New York Times
item.media:description: The University of Pennsylvania campus in Philadelphia.
